title: Authority of Scripture
definition: The authority of Scripture means that the Bible, as God's written Word, is the final and binding standard for what believers are to believe, teach, obey, and practice.
summary: Because Scripture is God's Word, it carries God's authority. The Bible is not merely helpful advice, religious tradition, or human opinion. It is the standard by which doctrine is tested, sin is exposed, faith is strengthened, and the church is instructed. Every teaching, experience, tradition, and spiritual claim must be submitted to the written Word of God.
christFocus: Jesus Christ honored, fulfilled, taught, and obeyed Scripture. He used the Word against temptation, explained the Scriptures concerning Himself, and prayed that His people would be sanctified by the truth. To submit to Scripture is not cold legalism; it is part of following Christ as Lord.

studySections.heading: Scripture as Final Standard
studySections.content: The authority of Scripture means that no church tradition, personal experience, teacher, feeling, or cultural pressure stands above God's Word. All doctrine and practice must be tested by Scripture.

studySections.heading: Scripture and Obedience
studySections.content: The Bible is not given merely to inform the mind but to shape the life. True submission to Scripture leads believers to repentance, faith, worship, holiness, love, and mission.

studySections.heading: Scripture and Discernment
studySections.content: The Bereans were commended because they examined the Scriptures daily to see whether what they heard was true. The authority of Scripture protects believers from deception and anchors them in God's revealed truth.
